correctness.rationale: Directly verify the hyperplane distance 1-t for z=(t,y) and the optimal witness (1,y). For every finite p the unit ball gives ||y||^p<=1-|t|^p; the distance ||x-z||^p is bounded by (1-t)^p+1-|t|^p. This envelope decreases with t in [-1,1], including the p=1 plateau, so the sharp slice radius is G_p(d)^(1/p). It is attained by z_d=(1-d,(1-|1-d|^p)^(1/p)u). Invert this radius to get eta; G_p is strictly increasing for p>1 and p=1 has a saturation at d=1. For p=infinity the exact radius is max(d,1), yielding a zero plateau at epsilon<=1. Endpoint and asymptotic claims follow from direct substitutions and G_p(d)=pd+o(d). This is an all-dimensions analytic argument; numeric tests are supplementary.
risks: Interpretation is the local pairwise index, not the global infimum.
Floating and rational finite test grids do not establish the continuum theorem.

originality.rationale: The 2023 defining PDF was inspected at the local-index definition, exact L2 Theorem 2.3, the particular ℓ-infinity endpoint calculation in Proposition 2.2, subsequent comparison index and general Lp-summand stereographic Theorem 2.6. The 2024 follow-up PDF was inspected at its index/core results, which provide different endpoint/qualitative criteria. Published semantic-literature searches covered exact eta symbols, polynomial envelope, ell_3^2 coordinate slices, Lp-summand support planes, singular endpoints and the p=2 pivot, without a covering exact non-Hilbert formula. A general support-functional reduction of eta supplies an abstract optimization identity, but it does not evaluate the scalar-summand profile; comparable published computations concern different moduli. The p=2 case is explicitly conceded as prior.
residual_risks: Indexing cannot prove absolute novelty, and a general local-uniform-convexity formula under a different name could imply the same scalar envelope.
The index is local at a single support pair; no global statement is asserted.
The original article already covers the p=2 specialization, which is not counted as new.

value.rationale: This is a sharp evaluation of an intrinsic, recently defined strong-exposure index for the natural class of scalar ell_p-summand vectors, uniformly across arbitrary nonzero Banach complements. It provides more than a point computation: every exposed-slice radius, every epsilon and p endpoint, attained extremizers, the exact local exposure order epsilon^p/p, a universal finite-p midpoint, and singular endpoint behavior at both p=1 and infinity. The source itself treats non-Hilbert p-summands qualitatively but lacks these quantitative benchmarks. These are motivated boundaries of a natural invariant rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
risks: The scalar-summand restriction is a natural tractable model but does not classify all support points in an arbitrary ell_p sum.
The p=2 reduction was previously proved.
